quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Try producing "jell" yourself. To make /dʒ/, you stop the air just behind your top teeth, then release it as a hiss, with your voice on — quite different from /j/, which needs you to raise the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth and glide, like starting to say "ee".
quests.explanation: This is /dʒ/, not /j/: in "jell", you stop the air just behind your top teeth, then release it as a hiss, with your voice on. The distractor would instead need raising the middle of your tongue toward the roof of your mouth and gliding, like starting to say "ee", which changes the sound completely.
quests.mouthPosition: Stop the air just behind your top teeth, then release it as a hiss, with your voice on.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Here's the key contrast in "dare": /d/ is made by tapping your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with your voice on, and /ð/ is made by placing your tongue tip lightly behind your top teeth and blowing with your voice on. Which description fits what you hear?
quests.explanation: "dare" is built on /d/ — tapping your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with your voice on is how it's made. That's a voiced alveolar plosive, easy to tell apart from the voiced dental fricative /ð/ once you know both feel different in the mouth.
quests.mouthPosition: To produce this sound, tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with your voice on.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
